findings.message: MCP tool annotations preserve effect hints, but clients must treat them as untrusted metadata.
The output schema advertises the receipt; durable audit storage belongs in the application handler.
Required actor and scopes are preserved in metadata; the generated handler must enforce them at runtime.
Confirmation is enforced through MCP elicitation; the SDK's compatibility layer also supports the next multi-round-trip input_required flow.
The idempotencyKey key is schema-visible; durable deduplication belongs in the application handler.
Contract scenarios become conformance-test inputs because MCP tool discovery has no behavioral scenario field.
Input and output JSON Schemas are emitted directly as MCP tool schemas.
